result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the same main problems: 11px script for the opening hours, hairline 13px body text, too many display faces, and no fallbacks. B goes further. It warns that digits in script faces are easy to misread, adds fallbacks to every font stack, and points out that the Google Fonts URL must change along with the weight. A's fix keeps the looping script Pacifico for all headings and the tagline, which is less legible than B's choice of a single bold display face for the h1 only. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the same core problems: the hairline 13px body text, the 11px script opening hours, too many display faces, and no fallbacks. A gives more detail on each one. It explains what happens on mobile when the fonts fail to load, and it points out that the Google Fonts URL has to change along with the weight. B is shorter and still solid, but it puts Pacifico, a script face, on every heading level, which is a weaker readability choice than A's single bold h1 with plain subheadings.
